subject: physics
question_text: Calculate the time needed for a net force of 5 N to change the velocity of a 10 kg mass by 2 m/s.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER (numerical). The 1+1 split — formula, then value — is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher. The arithmetic is hand-checked; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The formula
lines: Force = rate of change of momentum:

lines.text: F = m Δv / t   →   t = m Δv / F

steps.margin_note: Rearrange for t on its own line before putting any number in.
steps.why: Newton second law in its momentum form answers this directly — a force applied for a time changes momentum by F t.
common_mistakes: Multiplying instead of dividing, giving 100 s.

recall.must_convey: That t = m times the change in velocity, divided by F.
accept: t equals m delta v by F
force is rate of change of momentum
time is mass into change in velocity by force

steps.label: The value
steps.margin_note: One substitution line, then the boxed answer with its unit.
steps.why: A 5 N force adds 5 kg m/s of momentum every second; 20 kg m/s is needed, so it takes 4 seconds.
common_mistakes: Leaving the unit off the answer.

recall.must_convey: That the time works out to 4 seconds.
reject: t equals m delta v by F
